gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 can only use its full 1,000 W of solar input if the panel string runs at 50 V or more while its open-circuit voltage stays at 60 V or less. The input is capped at 20 A, and 1,000 W ÷ 20 A = 50 V. That narrow 50–60 V window controls how far you can grow the kit from its 200 W panel.
standout_why: I read backup-power.org/best-solar-generator-kits (cited), EnergySage's solar-generators overview (cited) and our own Dealectric page (cited), all on 2026-11-14. backup-power.org already prints the Elite 200 V2's raw '1,000 W at 12–60 V, 20 A' and the AC180's 12–60 V / 10 A cap. It also gives a series-wiring hint, but only for the AC180. For the Elite 200 V2 it says only that the 1,000 W input 'lets you keep adding panels', and our page says the same ('takes more panels later'). EnergySage has no voltage or current figures for any of these kits. None of the three works out the 50 V minimum string voltage or warns that a 60 V open-circuit limit limits how many panels can go in series. So rivals have the raw spec but not what it means for wiring, which is why this is a 1 and not a 2.
decides: This supports the Elite 200 V2 as the pick, since it has the biggest solar input of the candidates, but it adds a condition. Adding more 200 W panels is only possible within the 60 V open-circuit / 20 A window, and getting near 1,000 W needs a string running at 50 V or more. The page should say this rather than 'add panels later', and should link BLUETTI's 2×200 W kit ($1,499) as the easy step up. I couldn't open the SP200L's open-circuit voltage, so the exact maximum number of panels in series is still unsourced.

findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Portable Power Station | 2,600W 2,080Wh

findings.label: Minimum string operating voltage to reach the full 1,000 W solar input
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Portable Power Station | 2,600W 2,080Wh
findings.note: My arithmetic from the maker's spec: 1,000 W ÷ 20 A current cap = 50 V. Any array delivering under 50 V at its maximum-power point is held below 1,000 W by the 20 A cap, while its open-circuit voltage must stay at or below the 60 V ceiling. So the array has to run between 50 and 60 V to get the full 1,000 W.
